questions.question:

questions.solution: The correct answer is '**proliferation**' [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The given sentence is saying something about atomic weapons resulting in the danger of the survival of mankind. • The use of the word '**atomic weapons**' in the sentence means **weapons that derive their destructive power from the rapid release of nuclear energy**. (परमाणु हथियार) • Therefore, the most appropriate word to be filled in the blank is 'proliferation'. • **Proliferation** means **a rapid increase in the number or amount of something**. (संख्‍या में तेज़ी से बढ़ोतरी) • Example:* They worked to limit the **proliferation** of nuclear weapons and improve governmental efficiency*. Conclusion: The survival of mankind is in danger due to the rapid increase of atomic weapons. Hence, the correct answer is option 4. Complete Sentence: *The survival of mankind itself is in danger due to the proliferation of atomic weapons*. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** • Let us explore the other options: • **Perpetuation** means **the continuation or preservation of a situation, idea, etc**. (किसी स्थिति, विचार आदि की निरंतरता या संरक्षण) • **Regularization** means **to make agree with a single established standard or model**. (एक स्थापित मानक या मॉडल से सहमत) • **Provocation** means **action or speech that makes someone angry, especially deliberately**. (किसी को क्रोधित या परेशान करने के लिए जान-बूझकर की गई बात, हरकत आदि) 3a:T8db, The correct answer is- '**preoccupations.**'

questions.question:
Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the given idiom/phrase.

The straw that broke the camel's back

options.text: the smallest addition to an already heavy task makes it intolerable
a misery that can collapse even the strongest individual
a disease that can kill an animal

questions.solution:
The correct answer is- 'the smallest addition to an already heavy task makes it intolerable.' ***__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The meaning of the given idiom is:
 
• The straw that broke the camel's back means *the minor action that causes an unpredictably large and sudden reaction, because of the cumulative effect of small actions*. (छोटी-छोटी क्रियाओं के संचयी प्रभाव के कारण एक छोटी क्रिया जो अप्रत्याशित रूप से बड़ी और अचानक प्रतिक्रिया उत्पन्न करती हैं।)
 
 
• Example: **With governmental resources already strained to the breaking point, any sort of environmental disaster would be **the straw that breaks the camel's back**.*
 
 
 
• By the above meaning and example, we can say that 'the smallest addition to an already heavy task makes it intolerable' is the correct answer.

Hence *option 1 *is the appropriate answer. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Let's learn about the origin of the given idiom:
 
 
• This phrase came from a **story **that goes like this: "An Arabian story told of a camel whose owner loaded the beast of burden with as much straw as possible. Not satisfied with the staggering load he had put on the camel, the owner added just one last piece of straw. Even that one wisp was too much, and the animal collapsed with a broken back, leaving the owner with no way to take his goods to the market." The story is a parable for all the times you've been repeatedly irked until you can't take it anymore and you explode.

questions.question:
In the following question, a sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four alternatives suggested, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.

"Saint George help us!" exclaimed the Knight, "do the false yeomen give way?"

options.text: The Knight prayed that Saint George might help them and said that the false yeomen have been given away.
The Knight asked Saint George to help them and asked whether the false yeomen gave way.
The Knight prayed to Saint George to help them and asked whether the false yeomen gave way.
The Knight told Saint George to help them and questioned if the false yeomen gave way or not.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __O____ption 3)__ i.e. **The Knight prayed to Saint George to help them and asked whether the false yeomen gave way.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e97c856a86e7f9a2254b6d21594beffe8b2a2afbb0c5bd00cd60b251c8f9881c.png] Explanation:

While changing the narration of an exclamatory sentence, we need to follow the steps given below-

 
• Exclamatory sentences express a sudden outburst of some emotions such as joy, sorrow, contempt, regret, surprise etc. 
 
• In indirect speech, the exclamatory phrase or word (interjection) is replaced by ‘applauded, exclaimed with joy, sorrow, regret, surprise, contempt etc.
 
 
• Since the knight is praying to Saint to help him, **'prayed' **is the right word to use.
 
 
 
• The second statement is **interrogative**, so **'asked' **is used for the second statement.
 
• The connector 'that' is placed and semicolons and comma are removed for the first statement and for second **'whether/if' **should be placed.
 
• Pronoun **'us' **is replaced by **'them**' in indirect speech.
 
• The present indefinite tense in direct speech is changed into the **past indefinite** tense in indirect speech.

Thus, the sentence becomes: ***The Knight prayed to Saint George to help them and asked whether the false yeomen gave way.***

questions.question:
**A part of a sentence is underlined. Select the option which, when substituted for the underlined part will improve it. If no improvement is possible, select (D)**.

The fact-finding team __which had been at__ the area found the situation very grave.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4) i.e. No improvement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/52da89e0a2679b367562ad6c0d6e656a668762aeb60deda63544b7552771e3b0.png] Let's look at the explanation given below:

__
 
• The **noun **used just after the **underlined** part i.e. **area**, suggests that a particular **spot** has been talked about.
 
• In case of an **exact or a particular location**, the preposition **'at' **is used.
 
• The only option that follows the desired structure is the 4th option i.e.** No improvement.**

Correct Sentence__: *"**The fact-finding team **__which had been at__** the area found the situation very grave."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/50618910e2858de29bd243bf3e03a7eb28611b5a177e22623b53abcc6a893c97.png] Let's look at the difference between which and that:

 
• We use **which** is case of a **defining clause** whereas **that** is used for a **non-defining clause.**
 
• For example: 
 
 
• My bike** that **has a broken seat is in the garage.
 
• My bike, **which** has a broken seat, is in the garage.
 
 
 
• In the **1st **example, the subject may have** two or more **bikes and the particular bike is identifiable because of a **broken seat.**
 
• In the** 2ⁿd** example, the subject has only a **single bike **and the **broken seat **is simply a **description **of the bike in the garage.

questions.question:
**Select the correct the passive form of the given sentence.**

 Seema had to abstain him from smoking.

options.text: He had to be abstained from smoking by Seema.
He was made to abstained from smoking by her.

questions.solution:
The correct solution is option 3.

When changing from active to passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence and the subject of the active sentence becomes the object of the passive sentence (or is dropped).

We follow the order ”Subject + helping verb+ to be+ past participle+ by+ agent.

Here the verb is ‘abstain’ whose past participle is ‘abstained’.

‘had’ was used because ‘he’ is singular.

So, the correct answer is, “He had to be abstained from smoking by Seema.”
